title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that compares a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline against accepting an LLM candidate directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and validator, we selected K=200 tasks by a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule and used one shared generator output per task for both arms. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked (repair_applied=false for every guarded episode). All execution and scoring artifacts are archived (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6) to enable deterministic replay and reuse. The null/ceiling result is specific to the tested model/validator/task‑selection regime and does not imply verifier irrelevance in failure‑rich or production distributions; we discuss design lessons and reproducible next steps.

sections.introduction: Operator intent→configuration automation can increase agility but poses risks: improperly applied changes cause regressions (reachability loss, service interruption). Generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipelines are widely advocated to reduce such regressions by (i) generating candidate configuration commands with an LLM, (ii) verifying candidate semantics and safety with a deterministic validator, and (iii) repairing failing candidates before apply. Despite prototypes and position papers advocating this architecture, causal, preregistered estimates of the verifier’s marginal effect under reproducible sampling remain scarce. We preregistered (cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) and executed a paired experiment that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect by using a single shared initial generator output per task. Our primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired binary outcome). The run archive (execution/) preserves full model calls, validator traces, and scoring JSONs to enable deterministic replay.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and benchmarks discuss LLM‑assisted NetOps and generate–validate–repair patterns and emphasize verifier integration (e.g., Cornetto and related generate–validate–repair studies). Work advocating confining LLMs to translation and relying on solvers for reasoning is relevant for assay design. Our contribution is methodological and empirical: a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired causal estimate that isolates the verifier’s marginal contribution under a deterministic task selection and shared‑initial generation contract. We position this outcome as complementary to prior engineering prototypes and to papers that evaluate open‑loop LLM performance on configuration tasks.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We froze the experiment plan (cand-002-gvr-loop) before observing final outcomes. Design: paired binary comparison (baseline vs guarded) using deterministic selection of K=200 tasks. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on paired outcomes; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for a 95% percentile CI. Task population and sampling. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and filtered to those the preregistered deterministic validator covered (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). To avoid human selection, we used the preregistered deterministic selection rule: compute SHA‑256(intent_string), sort ascending, and take the first K=200 unique tasks (manifest: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b77621f83208298f5c8d965bcdbba115e741f95a1efb92944347b35bbf0). Shared initial generation and arms. For each task we produced exactly one shared_initial_generation candidate which both arms used unchanged. Baseline: accept candidate_c as the apply proposal and score post‑apply via the deterministic validator. Guarded: run candidate_c through the validator first; if it fails, allow at most one automated repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1). This shared‑initial design isolates verifier marginality on fixed generator outputs but prevents generator regeneration after validation feedback (a preregistered choice). Models and tooling. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Provenance and artifact capture. We archived every provider call, prompt/response, validator trace, scoring JSON, and per‑task metadata. Key artifact fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 = 79c91155..., analysis artifacts (paired contingency and condition summaries) are recorded (see Results and pointers below). Analysis plan for degenerate outcomes. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (~0.20). In paired designs, if no discordant pairs occur (n10=n01=0), the paired estimate is exactly zero; the exact McNemar p=1.00 and the bootstrap percentile CI may degenerate to a point mass. We executed the preregistered bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) and report the empirical (degenerate) result.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Planned episodes: 400 (200 tasks × 2 arms). Completed episodes: 400; model calls used: 200 (single shared initial generation per task); no repair calls were invoked (repair_applied=false for every guarded episode). No provider or infrastructure failures affected scientific data capture. Raw and scored artifacts are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline passes = 200/200; guarded passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference (guarded minus baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The paired contingency CSV and condition summary are archived: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Representative diagnostics and per‑task metadata. Every scoring JSON contains validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot, and difficulty metadata). Example artifacts: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874cebd979af0ded1859e51e6f51d937b5f9967d62c73f439aa52a257cc) and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = d10b415a1974c9ba846a31a0392edee2f117bae1a83411c984bed2d1d6c9411b). The manifest includes a small representative set whose difficulty composition was medium=1, hard=2, very_hard=3 (representative_tasks embedded in the archive). The full per‑task difficulty metadata for all K=200 tasks is present under execution/scoring/*.json and can be deterministically aggregated by replaying those JSONs; we deliberately preserved per‑task JSONs to enable independent audit rather than collapsing them during execution. Why repairs were not invoked. Artifact‑grounded reasons: (1) the preregistered inclusion rule required validator coverage, biasing the sample toward intents the validator supports; (2) gpt-5-mini generated candidates that conformed to the encoded workflow constraints in the task payloads (see per‑task normalized_configuration fields in execution/scoring/*.json); (3) the shared_initial_generation design fixes generator outputs and therefore allowed no generator adaptation in response to validator feedback so repairs could be invoked only when the fixed initial candidate failed validation. Reproducibility pointers. The run provides all artifacts needed to replay the exact analysis: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce925..., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4..., and the master prompt reference at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation. The observed ceiling (baseline = 100% pass rate) makes the preregistered power calculation (which assumed baseline ≈ 20%) inapplicable post hoc: exact paired inference and the bootstrap fully describe the observed data. When every pair is concordant (n11=200), the McNemar test yields p=1.00 and the paired bootstrap reproduces identical empirical pairs so the percentile CI collapses to a point [0.00,0.00]. This is the correct descriptive inference for the tested regime. Design implications for future verifier utility studies (artifact‑grounded guidance). To reliably measure verifier/repair marginal utility, future evaluations should: (i) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical misconfigurations or adversarial tasks) rather than requiring validator coverage for inclusion; (ii) vary generator capability (include weaker models) to produce nonzero baseline failure rates; (iii) evaluate alternate estimands that permit interactive regeneration (when the generator can adapt to validator feedback) rather than the shared_initial design used here; (iv) publish per‑task validator coverage and difficulty aggregates together with paired counts — our archive supplies per‑task difficulty metadata and validator traces to support such aggregation. Operational lessons from the artifacts. The run shows how deterministic validators can produce crisp binary outcomes and rich diagnostics (validation_before/after final_state snapshots, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count) that are sufficient for deterministic paired inference when failures exist; however, the benefit of a verifier in practice depends critically on selecting a task distribution where generators occasionally violate verifier constraints. Limitations that shape interpretation are enumerated below and in the archived manifest.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully artifact‑archived paired evaluation of a verifier+repair pipeline versus accepting LLM candidates directly under a deterministic sampling and shared_initial generation contract. Under the requested model (gpt-5-mini) and the preregistered validator coverage inclusion rule, all shared generator candidates passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair path was never invoked. This reproducible ceiling/null result (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...) is narrowly scoped to the tested model/validator/task regime and therefore does not generalize to failure‑rich production settings. We recommend future confirmatory evaluations intentionally sample or construct failure‑rich tasks, vary generator capabilities, and consider interactive closed‑loop estimands if the scientific goal is to measure end‑to‑end verifier utility. All execution artifacts and the master prompt reference are released for deterministic replay and audit (see Disclosure).

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Synthetic deterministic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) limit external validity to production intent distributions that contain emergent or historical misconfigurations.
Construct validity is tied to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; if the validator lacks coverage for real regression modes, the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
